title: Histological assessment of developmental cell death in Drosophila pupae
protocol: Collect white prepupae from the side wall of a culture vial using forceps and place them in a petri dish lined with wet tissue paper.
Incubate the WPP-containing petri dish in a 25°C incubator with a 16 h day/8 h night cycle for exactly 24 hours.
Submerge a pupa in a concave slide containing PBS.
Incise the pupal case first at the anterior end of the pupa and then at the posterior end.
Puncture the cuticle at the posterior end of the developing animal using the tip of dissecting scissors or a needle.
Transfer the pupae to an Eppendorf tube with 500 μL of fixative solution.
Incubate the pupae in fixative at 4°C for 48 hours.
Discard the fixative solution and add 500 μL of 80% ethanol to the pupae.
Rotate the pupae with ethanol on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 15 min.
Discard 80% ethanol and add 500 μL of 85% ethanol.
Rotate on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 20 min.
Discard 85% ethanol and add 500 μL of 90% ethanol.
Rotate on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 25 min.
Discard 90% ethanol and add 500 μL of 100% ethanol.
Rotate on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Discard 100% ethanol and add 500 μL of fresh 100% ethanol.
Rotate on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Repeat steps with 100% ethanol two additional times.
Discard the 100% ethanol from the tube and add 500 μL of 100% xylene.
Rotate on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Discard 100% xylene and add 500 μL of fresh 100% xylene.
Rotate on a nutator at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Repeat steps with 100% xylene two additional times.
In a 20 mL scintillation vial, add approximately 1.8 g of paraffin chips and 2 mL of 100% xylene.
Transfer the pupae into the scintillation vial containing melted paraffin and xylene mixture.
Note: Add a maximum of 20 animals per vial. If more animals have been collected from one genotype/condition, split them into an appropriate number of vials.
Incubate pupae in a 42°C incubator for 16-20 hours.
Discard the xylene/paraffin solution from the vial using a glass pipette.
Add an adequate amount of melted paraffin, enough to cover all of the pupae.
Incubate the vial containing the pupae in a 56°C incubator for 2 hours.
Replace melted paraffin with fresh melted paraffin and incubate in a 56°C incubator for 2 hours.
Repeat step (add fresh melted paraffin and incubate) two additional times.
Pause Point: The procedure can be paused for at least one week.
Fill the vial with melted paraffin.
Incubate the vial in a 56°C incubator for at least 30 minutes.
Make a mold using a 3" × 5" white unruled index card.
Pre-heat the mold on a slide warmer set to 56°C covered with aluminum foil.
Quickly pour the melted paraffin containing the pupae into the mold.
Orient the pupae using a toothpick with their ventral side facing down and spiracles pointing up.
Ensure there is an adequate amount of space between each pupa before the paraffin hardens.
Peel away the paper mold from the hardened paraffin block.
Cut the paraffin block into smaller individual pyramid-shaped blocks.
Mount a block on a microtome chuck by melting and solidifying the paraffin on the microtome chuck.
Trim the blocks to form a truncated rectangular pyramid with 0.5 mm of space surrounding the animals.
Place a microscope slide onto a 42°C slide warmer.
Add distilled water on top of the microscope slide.
Use a microtome to cut sections at 7 μm thickness.
Float the sections onto a microscope slide with water.
Let the sections expand for 1–2 minutes.
Remove excess water from the slides using a paper towel along the side.
Place the slides on a 42°C slide warmer for 16–20 hours.
Incubate the tissue sequentially in containers containing: 100% Xylene I for 3 minutes.
Incubate the tissue sequentially in containers containing: 100% Xylene II for 3 minutes.
Incubate the tissue sequentially in containers containing: 100% Ethanol I for 3 minutes.
Incubate tissue sections in 100% ethanol II for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 95% ethanol I for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 75% ethanol for 3 min.
Rinse tissue sections with running tap water for 5 min.
Stain tissue sections with Weigert’s Hematoxylin for 5 min.
Rinse tissue sections with running tap water for 5 min.
Stain tissue sections with Pollak’s Trichrome for 7 min.
Rinse tissue sections in distilled water for 10 s.
Rinse tissue sections in 0.2% glacial acetic acid in distilled water for 10 s.
Dehydrate tissue sections by dipping in 70% ethanol 2–3 times.
Incubate tissue sections in 95% ethanol II for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 95% ethanol I for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 100% ethanol I for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 100% ethanol II for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 100% xylene II for 3 min.
Incubate tissue sections in 100% xylene I for 3 min.
Dry slides on a paper towel for 3 min.
Apply approximately 80 μL of Permount per slide.
Mount a 50 mm coverslip on the sections.
Leave slides on a cardboard slide tray at 20°C–25°C for at least 2 hours for the Permount to partially harden.
Acquire representative images from each genotype/condition using a brightfield microscope with a 5× objective.
Store slides in a slide box indefinitely once Permount has completely hardened after 24–48 hours.
